title: Reinforced Concrete Design
description: Reinforced Concrete Design is a senior civil elective emphasizing ACI-based strength design, member analysis, detailing, serviceability, and constructability for beams, slabs, columns, foundations, and frames.

topics.title: Properties of Concrete and Reinforcing Steel
topics.description: Establishes how concrete and steel behave separately and together, including strength, stiffness, strain compatibility, durability, and variability.

children.title: Concrete behavior
children.description: Students learn why concrete is strong in compression, weak in tension, and sensitive to curing, cracking, creep, shrinkage, and durability conditions.

children.title: Reinforcing steel behavior
children.description: Steel provides reliable tensile strength and ductility when it is properly placed, developed, and protected.

children.title: Composite action
children.description: Reinforced concrete design depends on strain compatibility, bond, and force equilibrium between concrete and steel.

topics.title: Strength Design Philosophy and ACI 318 Framework
topics.description: Introduces the limit-state design approach used by ACI 318, including load combinations, strength reduction factors, ductility, and safety margins.

children.title: Limit states and design strength
children.description: Students distinguish nominal strength, design strength, factored loads, and acceptable performance.

children.title: Load combinations
children.description: Load combinations organize gravity, lateral, environmental, and service loads into code-checkable cases.

children.title: Code workflow
children.description: Students learn to navigate ACI-style design checks rather than treating formulas as disconnected recipes.

topics.title: Flexural Analysis and Design of Beams
topics.description: Develops the most central RC member design skill: computing moment strength and selecting reinforcement for ductile beam behavior.

children.title: Section analysis
children.description: Students calculate moment capacity using equilibrium, strain compatibility, and equivalent stress blocks.

children.title: Beam design
children.description: Design turns a required factored moment into bar selection, spacing, cover, and practical detailing.

children.title: Ductility and failure behavior
children.description: Students learn to favor ductile flexural yielding rather than brittle compression or shear failures.

topics.title: Shear Design
topics.description: Explains how diagonal cracking and shear transfer mechanisms are checked and reinforced so beams do not fail suddenly.

children.title: Shear behavior
children.description: Students learn why shear cracking is different from flexural cracking and often more brittle.

children.title: Concrete and steel shear strength
children.description: Design separates nominal concrete contribution from transverse reinforcement contribution.

children.title: Detailing for shear
children.description: Students connect calculations to stirrup layout, anchorage, spacing zones, and constructability.

topics.title: Development Length, Anchorage, and Bar Splices
topics.description: Shows how reinforcement actually develops force through bond, hooks, embedment, and splice detailing.

children.title: Bond and development
children.description: Students learn why a bar must extend far enough beyond a critical section to reach its design stress.

children.title: Anchorage and hooks
children.description: Anchorage details help transfer forces when straight embedment is not sufficient or space is limited.

children.title: Splices and continuity
children.description: Splices let reinforcement continue through real construction lengths while preserving force transfer.

topics.title: Serviceability, Cracking, and Deflection
topics.description: Adds the usability side of design: members must not only be strong, but also control deflection, cracking, vibration, and long-term deformation.

children.title: Crack control
children.description: Students learn how bar spacing, cover, tension stress, and detailing influence visible cracking.

children.title: Deflection control
children.description: Deflection checks protect function, finishes, partitions, drainage, and user perception.

children.title: Time-dependent effects
children.description: Concrete continues to deform after loading, making creep and shrinkage important in serviceability.

topics.title: One-Way and Two-Way Slabs
topics.description: Extends flexural design to floor systems, where load paths, support conditions, distribution reinforcement, and punching behavior matter.

children.title: One-way slab design
children.description: One-way slabs behave like wide beams spanning primarily in one direction.

children.title: Two-way slab behavior
children.description: Two-way systems distribute load in both directions and require attention to support layout and moment transfer.

children.title: Punching shear
children.description: Slabs around columns can fail by punching, requiring local checks and sometimes shear reinforcement.

topics.title: Columns: Axial and Combined Loading
topics.description: Covers compression members subjected to axial load and bending, including interaction behavior, slenderness, confinement, and detailing.

children.title: Short column capacity
children.description: Students learn the basic axial strength model for tied and spiral columns.

children.title: Axial-flexural interaction
children.description: Most columns carry axial load and moment together, so design uses interaction thinking rather than one isolated formula.

children.title: Slenderness and detailing
children.description: Column performance depends on stability, confinement, bar spacing, ties, and constructability.

topics.title: Footings and Foundations
topics.description: Connects member design to soil-supported elements that spread column and wall loads safely into the ground.

children.title: Isolated footing design
children.description: Students design footing dimensions and reinforcement to satisfy bearing, flexure, and shear.

children.title: Combined and strap footings
children.description: More complex footing systems address property lines, eccentric loads, and multiple columns.

children.title: Detailing and constructability
children.description: Foundation drawings require clear cover, dowels, development, and coordination with geotechnical assumptions.

topics.title: Walls, Retaining Walls, and Lateral Members
topics.description: Broadens the course from beams and columns to vertical members resisting soil pressure, gravity loads, and lateral forces.

children.title: Structural walls
children.description: Structural walls resist axial load, bending, and shear in buildings and can be central to lateral systems.

children.title: Retaining walls
children.description: Retaining wall design combines soil pressure, stability, flexure, shear, and drainage details.

children.title: Lateral load path
children.description: Students connect RC member design to diaphragms, frames, walls, and foundations.

topics.title: Frames and Seismic Considerations
topics.description: Introduces ductile reinforced concrete frame behavior and seismic detailing principles without turning the course into a full earthquake engineering sequence.

children.title: Frame behavior
children.description: Frames distribute moments and shears through beams, columns, joints, and foundations.

children.title: Ductile detailing
children.description: Seismic performance relies on confinement, continuity, and preventing brittle failure mechanisms.

children.title: Performance and code context
children.description: Students learn the purpose of seismic design categories and detailing requirements at a conceptual level.

topics.title: Prestressed and Precast Concrete Awareness
topics.description: Provides enough prestressed and precast context for students to recognize when ordinary RC assumptions change and when specialized design is needed.

children.title: Prestressing principles
children.description: Prestressing places concrete in compression to improve service behavior and span capability.

children.title: Prestressed member behavior
children.description: Students compare flexure, cracking, deflection, and shear in prestressed members against ordinary RC members.

children.title: Precast systems
children.description: Precast concrete introduces plant production, connections, transportation, erection, and tolerances.

topics.title: Detailing, Construction, and Design Documentation
topics.description: Closes the course by translating calculations into buildable drawings, schedules, details, and design narratives.

children.title: Reinforcement detailing
children.description: Good detailing makes the design constructible and protects the assumptions used in calculations.

children.title: Construction considerations
children.description: Students learn how formwork, placement, consolidation, curing, tolerances, and inspection affect structural performance.

children.title: Design documentation
children.description: Final deliverables must show assumptions, loads, calculations, code checks, and drawings clearly enough for review.
